# The Colors That Dance at the Edge of Night

## Scripture

*"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge."* — Psalm 19:1–2 (NIV)

## Reflection

On certain cold nights, far from city lights, the northern sky comes alive with color—pale greens and soft violets rippling across the darkness. The aurora borealis. We didn't paint those lights. We can't summon them. They appear only when solar winds meet Earth's magnetic field, and even then, only for those willing to stand in the cold and look up.

There's something quietly humbling about beauty we cannot manufacture. So much of our world is engineered, scheduled, controlled. But the aurora keeps its own counsel. It reminds us that God's glory is not a resource we manage—it is a gift we receive. The heavens "pour forth speech," the psalmist says, but they do so on their own terms, in their own time.

Perhaps tonight you feel the cold more than the color. Perhaps the sky above you looks ordinary. But the same God who choreographs lights across the Arctic is at work in the ordinary dark of your life, arranging glories you cannot yet see. He does not ask you to produce His beauty—only to stand, watch, and trust that it will come.

## Prayer

Lord of the heavens, thank You for beauty we cannot manufacture and grace we cannot earn. When our nights feel ordinary, help us keep watching, trusting that Your glory will appear in Your perfect time. Amen.
